1	"""Persistent storage: blockchain, pending set and derived indexes (JSON).
2	
3	The whole state is one JSON document written atomically: a uniquely named
4	``.ledger-*`` snapshot is fsynced in the same directory and then promoted over
5	the main file with ``os.replace`` (followed by a directory fsync). Every
6	successful write advances a monotonic ``generation`` recorded in the
7	snapshot. A crash can therefore only leave behind (a) the previous main file
8	or (b) a fully fsynced snapshot that never got renamed — never a torn file.
9	
10	On startup the main file and every sibling ``.ledger-*`` snapshot are treated
11	as recovery candidates. When no file exists at all, the unique genesis block
12	is created; otherwise each candidate is strictly validated (JSON, generation,
13	consecutive heights, prev_hash linkage, recomputed block hashes and Merkle
14	roots, per-transaction tx_id and Ed25519 signature, pending-only-at-tip and
15	mempool/chain de-duplication). The valid snapshot with the highest generation
16	wins and is promoted if it is still a temp file; same-generation content
17	conflicts, or a directory with no valid candidate, raise StateRecoveryError
18	with the offending path and reason — a fresh chain is never silently created.
19	
20	One atomic write persists everything: the chain (each block carries its
21	confirm/rollback ``status``), a small ``state`` summary, the mempool
22	(``pending``), candidate fork chains (``forks``, each a full block list
23	anchored at the canonical genesis and keyed by its tip hash), the
24	confirmed-transaction ``index`` and the confirmed ``accounts`` activity.
25	Derived data (index/accounts) is *rebuilt* from the chain on every load and
26	every save — pending blocks are excluded, so a restart never resurrects
27	unconfirmed transactions into balances. Persisted fork candidates are
28	re-validated on startup and invalid ones are dropped, while canonical-chain
29	invalidity remains fatal. Each surviving sync record carries the tip summary
30	(height/length/status) frozen at reception; a persisted frozen summary that
31	disagrees with the re-resolved candidate invalidates the record, while a
32	snapshot predating the feature is repaired from its candidate. Persisted sync
33	records are re-verified on restart:
34	records still unexpired whose source stays active and unexpired survive;
35	records whose own deadline elapsed or whose source is unknown/revoked/
36	registry-expired while the process was down are pruned (their non-adopted
37	forks removed; an adopted tip never changes the canonical chain) and each
38	gets exactly one sync_expired audit event backfilled after the durable
39	history, persisted in one atomic write. The backfill deduplicates only
40	within the record's current lifecycle (a durable sync_expired newer than
41	the key's latest sync_received), so a reused (source, request_id) key's
42	new lifecycle is always audited even when every field matches a previous
43	lifecycle's event. Other staleness (a dangling
44	tip or a content-fingerprint mismatch) is a silent prune with no event.
45	A re-entrant lock serializes all updates, and a class-wide recovery lock
46	serializes startup scans against in-flight writes.
47	"""

94	class SyncSummary:
95	    """Resolve the frozen tip descriptor (height/length/status) for a synced
96	    candidate during recovery, from either a surviving fork or a canonical
97	    chain prefix.
98	    """
99	
100	    @staticmethod
101	    def from_blocks_raw(tip_hash: str, blocks_raw: list[dict]) -> dict | None:
102	        """Build the descriptor for an already-resolved raw block list whose
103	        last block hash must equal ``tip_hash``.
104	        """
105	        if not blocks_raw:
106	            return None
107	        tip = blocks_raw[-1]
108	        if tip.get("block_hash") != tip_hash:
109	            return None
110	        return {
111	            "height": tip["height"],
112	            "length": len(blocks_raw),
113	            "status": tip["status"],
114	        }
115	
116	    @classmethod
117	    def from_locations(
118	        cls,
119	        tip_hash: str,
120	        forks: dict[str, list[Block]],
121	        canonical_chain: list[Block],
122	    ) -> dict | None:
123	        """Resolve a descriptor among surviving forks first, then canonical
124	        blocks (the delivered fork may since have been adopted).
125	        """
126	        fork = forks.get(tip_hash)
127	        if fork is not None:
128	            return cls.from_blocks_raw(tip_hash, [block.to_dict() for block in fork])
129	        prefix: list[dict] = []
130	        for block in canonical_chain:
131	            prefix.append(block.to_dict())
132	            if block.block_hash == tip_hash:
133	                return cls.from_blocks_raw(tip_hash, prefix)
134	        return None

152	class LedgerStore:
153	    def __init__(self, path: str, initial_balance: int | None = None) -> None:
154	        self.path = path
155	        self.chain: list[Block] = []
156	        self.pending: dict[str, Transaction] = {}
157	        # Candidate fork chains keyed by tip block hash. Each value is the
158	        # fork's full block list (including the shared genesis block).
159	        self.forks: dict[str, list[Block]] = {}
160	        # Inter-node sync submissions keyed by (source, request_id). Each
161	        # record stores delivery metadata plus the tip hash of the synced
162	        # candidate chain (kept in ``forks``) and a content fingerprint used
163	        # for same-key retry/idempotency checks.
164	        self.syncs: dict[tuple[str, str], dict] = {}
165	        # Persistent source-trust registry keyed by source identifier. Each

167	        self.trust_sources: dict[str, dict] = {}
168	        # Keyless trust allowlist {source: expires_at}; preserved verbatim and
169	        # surfaced by GET /v1/trust for offline light clients.
170	        self.allowlist: dict[str, int] = {}
171	        # Append-only audit events, each {"event_id", "kind", "at",
172	        # "prev_hash", "event_hash", ...payload}. event_id is the 1-based
173	        # position in this list; the two hash fields form a SHA-256 chain
174	        # anchored at 64 zeroes.
175	        self.audit_events: list[dict] = []
176	        # Head of the audit hash chain: {"event_id", "event_hash"} of the last
177	        # event, or {0, "0"*64} for an empty log. Persisted in every snapshot.
178	        self.audit_checkpoint: dict = audit.make_checkpoint([])
179	        # Rotatable Ed25519 checkpoint signer: the current
180	        # {"version", "private_key", "public_key"} or None on a legacy
181	        # unsigned snapshot until its one-time migration. Version 1 is
182	        # generated when the node is first created; rotation replaces the
183	        # whole record.
184	        self.audit_signer: dict | None = None
185	        # Every signer version ever held, oldest first, each
186	        # {"version", "public_key", "activated_event_id"}; version 1 is
187	        # activated at event 0, each later version at its
188	        # audit_signer_rotated event id. Public keys are retained forever so
189	        # historical checkpoints stay verifiable offline.
190	        self.audit_signer_history: list[dict] = []
191	        # Per-identity endowment used for candidate replay checks; recorded in
192	        # the snapshot so recovery validates against the same convention.
193	        self.initial_balance: int | None = initial_balance
194	        # Monotonic counter bumped on every successful atomic write. It is
195	        # persisted with each snapshot and lets startup pick the newest one.
196	        self.generation: int = 0
197	        # Derived, confirmed-only views; rebuilt by rebuild_derived().
198	        self.tx_index: dict[str, int] = {}
199	        self.accounts: dict[str, dict] = {}
200	        self._lock = threading.RLock()
201	        self.load()
202	
203	    @property
204	    def lock(self) -> threading.RLock:
205	        return self._lock
206	
207	    # Serializes startup scans/promotions between threads (or two store
208	    # instances on the same path) within one process. All later mutations take
209	    # the per-store re-entrant lock.
210	    _recovery_lock = threading.RLock()
211	
212	    def load(self) -> None:
213	        """Recover state from disk on startup.
214	
215	        The main file *and* every sibling ``.ledger-*`` snapshot are treated
216	        as recovery candidates. When none exist at all, the unique genesis
217	        block is created (the established first-start convention); otherwise
218	        every candidate is strictly validated and the valid snapshot with the
219	        highest generation wins. A winning temp snapshot is atomically
220	        promoted over the main file and every judged-older or residual
221	        candidate is removed. Same-generation snapshots with conflicting
222	        content, or a directory with no valid candidate, raise
223	        StateRecoveryError — a fresh chain is never silently created.
224	        """
225	        directory = os.path.dirname(os.path.abspath(self.path)) or "."
226	        with self._recovery_lock:
227	            candidates = self._discover_candidates(directory)
228	            if not candidates:
229	                os.makedirs(directory, exist_ok=True)
230	                self.chain = [self.create_genesis()]
231	                self.pending = {}
232	                self.forks = {}
233	                self.syncs = {}
234	                self.trust_sources = {}
235	                self.allowlist = {}
236	                self.audit_events = []
237	                self.audit_checkpoint = audit.make_checkpoint([])
238	                # A brand-new node mints its version 1 checkpoint key; the
239	                # first signer is activated at event 0 (the empty log).
240	                self.audit_signer = self._make_audit_signer(1, 0)
241	                self.audit_signer_history = [self._public_signer_entry(self.audit_signer)]
242	                self.generation = 0
243	                self.rebuild_derived()
244	                self.save()
245	                return
246	
247	            valid: list[tuple] = []
248	            errors: list[StateRecoveryError] = []
249	            for candidate in candidates:
250	                try:
251	                    data = self._read_candidate(candidate)
252	                    parsed = self._parse_snapshot(candidate, data)
253	                except StateRecoveryError as exc:
254	                    errors.append(exc)
255	                    continue
256	                # parsed = (chain, pending, generation, forks, initial_balance,
257	                #           syncs, trust_sources, allowlist, audit_events,
258	                #           expired_records, audit_checkpoint, audit_repair,
259	                #           signer_state)
260	                valid.append(
261	                    (
262	                        parsed[2],
263	                        candidate,
264	                        parsed[0],
265	                        parsed[1],
266	                        parsed[3],
267	                        parsed[4],
268	                        parsed[5],
269	                        parsed[6],
270	                        parsed[7],
271	                        parsed[8],
272	                        parsed[9],
273	                        parsed[10],
274	                        parsed[11],
275	                        parsed[12],
276	                    )
277	                )
278	
279	            if not valid:
280	                details = "; ".join(f"{exc.path} ({exc.reason})" for exc in errors)
281	                raise StateRecoveryError(
282	                    directory, f"no valid snapshot candidate found: {details}"
283	                )
284	
285	            max_generation = max(item[0] for item in valid)
286	            top = [item for item in valid if item[0] == max_generation]
287	            # item layout: (generation, path, chain, pending, forks,
288	            # initial_balance, syncs, trust_sources, allowlist, audit_events,
289	            # expired_records, audit_checkpoint, audit_repair, signer_state)
290	            reference = self._canonical_view(
291	                top[0][2],
292	                top[0][3],
293	                top[0][4],
294	                top[0][6],
295	                top[0][7],
296	                top[0][8],
297	                top[0][9],
298	                top[0][5],
299	                top[0][11],
300	                top[0][13][1],
301	            )
302	            for item in top[1:]:
303	                if (
304	                    self._canonical_view(
305	                        item[2],
306	                        item[3],
307	                        item[4],
308	                        item[6],
309	                        item[7],
310	                        item[8],
311	                        item[9],
312	                        item[5],
313	                        item[11],
314	                        item[13][1],
315	                    )
316	                    != reference
317	                ):
318	                    paths = " vs ".join(item[1] for item in top)
319	                    raise StateRecoveryError(
320	                        directory,
321	                        f"conflicting snapshots at generation {max_generation}: {paths}",
322	                    )
323	
324	            # Identical same-generation snapshots: keep the main file when it
325	            # is one of them, avoiding a pointless promotion cycle.
326	            main_abs = os.path.abspath(self.path)
327	            winner = top[0]
328	            for item in top:
329	                if os.path.abspath(item[1]) == main_abs:
330	                    winner = item
331	                    break
332	            (
333	                generation,
334	                winner_path,
335	                chain,
336	                pending,
337	                forks,
338	                winner_init_balance,
339	                syncs,
340	                trust_sources,
341	                allowlist,
342	                audit_events,
343	                expired_records,
344	                audit_checkpoint,
345	                audit_repair,
346	                signer_state,
347	            ) = winner
348	
349	            if os.path.abspath(winner_path) != main_abs:
350	                # The newest durable state only ever made it to a temp
351	                # snapshot (a crash interrupted the promotion): promote it.
352	                os.replace(winner_path, self.path)
353	                self._fsync_dir(directory)
354	
355	            # Reconcile records that expired or lost authorization while the
356	            # process was down, once, on the single winning snapshot: append
357	            # deduplicated sync_expired events with ids continuing after the
358	            # durable history. Doing this after same-generation conflict
359	            # detection keeps that comparison based on durable content (the
360	            # backfill carries a current timestamp).
361	            backfilled = self._backfill_expired_events(audit_events, expired_records)
362	            # A snapshot written before audit hash chaining carries no links;
363	            # expiry backfill events are likewise appended without hashes. In
364	            # both cases the single winning snapshot's log is (re)linked here:
365	            # renumbering dense ids and recomputing reproduces every already
366	            # validated link byte-for-byte and completes the new tail. A
367	            # present-but-wrong chain never reaches this point —
368	            # _parse_snapshot rejects it with StateRecoveryError.
369	            if audit_repair or backfilled:
370	                audit_events = audit.link_events(audit_events)
371	            audit_checkpoint = audit.make_checkpoint(audit_events)
372	
373	            # A pre-checkpoint-auth snapshot carries no signer at all: mint
374	            # its version 1 key once, here, on the unique winner (the
375	            # same-generation conflict comparison above already ran on the
376	            # durable candidates, exactly as for the hash-chain repair). The
377	            # new key is persisted atomically together with the (possibly
378	            # relinked) log and checkpoint in the single save() below.
379	            audit_signer, signer_history, signer_migration = signer_state
380	            if signer_migration:
381	                audit_signer = self._make_audit_signer(1, 0)
382	                signer_history = [self._public_signer_entry(audit_signer)]
383	
384	            self.chain = chain
385	            self.pending = pending
386	            self.forks = forks
387	            self.syncs = syncs
388	            self.trust_sources = trust_sources
389	            self.allowlist = allowlist
390	            self.audit_events = audit_events
391	            self.audit_checkpoint = audit_checkpoint
392	            self.audit_signer = audit_signer
393	            self.audit_signer_history = signer_history
394	            self.generation = generation
395	            # Prefer the endowment recorded by the writer; fall back to the
396	            # value this instance was constructed with, and finally to the
397	            # service default, so older snapshots without the field still
398	            # validate fork replays against the configured endowment.
399	            if winner_init_balance is not None:
400	                self.initial_balance = winner_init_balance
401	            self.rebuild_derived()
402	            self._cleanup_candidates(directory)
403	            # Persist the reconciled state (pruned records/forks + backfilled
404	            # events + legacy hash-chain completion + signer migration)
405	            # atomically so the next restart never re-derives or duplicates
406	            # anything; with nothing to reconcile no write happens and the
407	            # recovered generation is kept byte-for-byte.
408	            if backfilled or audit_repair or signer_migration:
409	                self.save()
410	
411	    def _discover_candidates(self, directory: str) -> list[str]:
412	        """List the main file and sibling .ledger-* snapshots (if any)."""
413	        candidates: list[str] = []
414	        if os.path.exists(self.path):
415	            candidates.append(self.path)
416	        try:
417	            names = sorted(os.listdir(directory))
418	        except OSError:
419	            return candidates
420	        main_name = os.path.basename(self.path)
421	        for name in names:
422	            if name == main_name or not name.startswith(SNAPSHOT_PREFIX):
423	                continue
424	            full = os.path.join(directory, name)
425	            if os.path.isfile(full):
426	                candidates.append(full)
427	        return candidates

429	    @staticmethod
430	    def _canonical_view(
431	        chain: list[Block],
432	        pending: dict[str, Transaction],
433	        forks: dict[str, list[Block]],
434	        syncs: dict[tuple[str, str], dict] | None = None,
435	        trust_sources: dict[str, dict] | None = None,
436	        allowlist: dict[str, int] | None = None,
437	        audit_events: list[dict] | None = None,
438	        initial_balance: int | None = None,
439	        audit_checkpoint: dict | None = None,
440	        audit_signer_history: list[dict] | None = None,
441	    ) -> str:
442	        """Order-independent canonical content hash for conflict detection.
443	
444	        The recorded ``initial_balance`` is part of the authoritative view: two
445	        same-generation snapshots with identical chains but a different
446	        endowment describe a different replay judgment and must conflict. The
447	        audit checkpoint participates too: two same-generation snapshots with
448	        the same events but a different log head disagree about the audited
449	        state and must conflict. The audit signer history (version, public key,
450	        activation event) participates as well, so a checkpoint key that
451	        differs between two same-generation snapshots is a conflict.
452	        """
453	        sync_records = [
454	            {
455	                "source": key[0],
456	                "request_id": key[1],
457	                "tip_hash": rec["tip_hash"],
458	                "expires_at": rec["expires_at"],
459	                "fingerprint": rec["fingerprint"],
460	                "height": rec.get("height"),
461	                "length": rec.get("length"),
462	                "status": rec.get("status"),
463	                # A range delivery's {anchor, blocks} payload participates in
464	                # conflict detection: same-generation snapshots disagreeing
465	                # about the delivered increment are a conflict.
466	                "range": rec.get("range"),
467	            }
468	            for key, rec in sorted((syncs or {}).items())
469	        ]
470	        trust_records = [
471	            {"source": source, **rec}
472	            for source, rec in sorted((trust_sources or {}).items())
473	        ]
474	        return json.dumps(
475	            {
476	                "initial_balance": initial_balance,
477	                "chain": [block.to_dict() for block in chain],
478	                "pending": [pending[tx_id].to_dict() for tx_id in sorted(pending)],
479	                "forks": [
480	                    [block.to_dict() for block in forks[tip]]
481	                    for tip in sorted(forks)
482	                ],
483	                "syncs": sync_records,
484	                "trust_sources": trust_records,
485	                "allowlist": dict(sorted((allowlist or {}).items())),
486	                "audit_events": audit_events or [],
487	                "audit_checkpoint": audit_checkpoint
488	                or {"event_id": 0, "event_hash": "0" * 64},
489	                "audit_signer_history": audit_signer_history or [],
490	            },
491	            sort_keys=True,
492	            ensure_ascii=False,
493	        )
494	
495	    def _cleanup_candidates(self, directory: str) -> None:
496	        """Remove every residual .ledger-* snapshot next to the main file.
497	
498	        After recovery these are by definition unusable leftovers: older
499	        generations, an identical post-promotion residue, or a partially
500	        written (invalid) file. The promoted/main state is never touched.
501	        """
502	        main_name = os.path.basename(self.path)
503	        for name in list(os.listdir(directory)):
504	            if not name.startswith(SNAPSHOT_PREFIX) or name == main_name:
505	                continue
506	            full = os.path.join(directory, name)
507	            try:
508	                if os.path.isfile(full) or os.path.islink(full):
509	                    os.unlink(full)
510	            except OSError:
511	                pass
512	        self._fsync_dir(directory)
513	
514	    @staticmethod
515	    def _read_candidate(path: str) -> dict:
516	        """Read and JSON-decode one snapshot file.
517	
518	        Any I/O or JSON failure becomes a StateRecoveryError carrying the
519	        offending path, never a silent fall-back.
520	        """
521	        try:
522	            with open(path, "r", encoding="utf-8") as fh:
523	                data = json.load(fh)
524	        except OSError as exc:
525	            raise StateRecoveryError(path, f"cannot read file: {exc}") from exc
526	        except (ValueError, UnicodeDecodeError) as exc:
527	            raise StateRecoveryError(path, f"invalid JSON: {exc}") from exc
528	        if not isinstance(data, dict):
529	            raise StateRecoveryError(path, "snapshot root must be a JSON object")
530	        return data
531	
532	    def _parse_snapshot(
533	        self, path: str, data: dict
534	    ) -> tuple[
535	        list[Block],
536	        dict[str, Transaction],
537	        int,
538	        dict[str, list[Block]],
539	        int | None,
540	        dict[tuple[str, str], dict],
541	        dict[str, dict],
542	        dict[str, int],
543	        list[dict],
544	        list[tuple[str, str, dict]],
545	        dict,
546	        bool,
547	        tuple[dict | None, list[dict], bool],
548	    ]:
549	        """Strictly validate one decoded snapshot.
550	
551	        Checks the persisted generation, consecutive heights, prev_hash
552	        linkage, recomputed block hashes, recomputed Merkle roots, every
553	        transaction's tx_id and Ed25519 signature, the pending-only-at-tip
554	        rule, and de-duplication between mempool and chain. Returns the parsed
555	        chain, mempool, generation, candidate forks and the recorded initial
556	        balance. Raises StateRecoveryError on the first defect, with ``path``
557	        identifying the candidate.
558	        """
559	        def fail(reason: str) -> None:
560	            raise StateRecoveryError(path, reason)
561	
562	        chain_raw = data.get("chain")
563	        if not isinstance(chain_raw, list) or not chain_raw:
564	            fail("snapshot must contain a non-empty chain")
565	
566	        state = data.get("state")
567	        # A pre-state-section snapshot is accepted: the chain itself is fully
568	        # self-verifying below. A present non-object section is corruption.
569	        if state is None:
570	            state = {}
571	        if not isinstance(state, dict):
572	            fail("invalid 'state' section: must be a JSON object")
573	        generation = state.get("generation", 0)
574	        # bool is an int subclass; reject it explicitly along with negatives.
575	        if isinstance(generation, bool) or not isinstance(generation, int) or generation < 0:
576	            fail("state.generation must be a non-negative integer")
577	        # Schema version gating the one-time pre-checkpoint-auth migration: a
578	        # snapshot written by current code always carries state.version >= 9,
579	        # so a present signer section is mandatory there; only a snapshot whose
580	        # version explicitly predates 9 may lack the signer sections at all.
581	        state_version = state.get("version")
582	        if state_version is not None and (
583	            isinstance(state_version, bool)
584	            or not isinstance(state_version, int)
585	            or state_version < 1
586	        ):
587	            fail("state.version must be a positive integer")
588	        initial_balance = state.get("initial_balance")
589	        if initial_balance is not None and (
590	            isinstance(initial_balance, bool)
591	            or not isinstance(initial_balance, int)
592	            or initial_balance <= 0
593	        ):
594	            fail("state.initial_balance must be a positive integer")
595	
596	        chain: list[Block] = []
597	        seen_tx_ids: set[str] = set()
598	        for i, block_raw in enumerate(chain_raw):
599	            if not isinstance(block_raw, dict):
600	                fail(f"block at position {i} is not a JSON object")
601	            try:
602	                block = Block.from_dict(block_raw)
603	            except (KeyError, TypeError, ValueError) as exc:
604	                fail(f"block {i} is malformed: {exc}")
605	            if block.height != i:
606	                fail(
607	                    f"block at position {i} has non-consecutive height "
608	                    f"{block.height}"
609	                )
610	            expected_prev = GENESIS_PREV_HASH if i == 0 else chain[i - 1].block_hash
611	            if block.prev_hash != expected_prev:
612	                fail(f"block {block.height} has a mismatched prev_hash")
613	            if block.status not in (STATUS_PENDING, STATUS_CONFIRMED):
614	                fail(f"block {block.height} has unknown status {block.status!r}")
615	            if i == 0 and (
616	                block.status != STATUS_CONFIRMED or block.transactions
617	            ):
618	                fail("genesis block must be confirmed and carry no transactions")
619	            # Pending blocks may only sit at the chain tip.
620	            if i < len(chain_raw) - 1 and block.status == STATUS_PENDING:
621	                fail(f"pending block {block.height} is not the chain tip")
622	
623	            # Validate every transaction: stored tx_id, recomputed tx_id and
624	            # the Ed25519 signature.
625	            tx_ids: list[str] = []
626	            txs_raw = block_raw.get("transactions")
627	            if not isinstance(txs_raw, list):
628	                fail(f"block {block.height} transactions must be a list")
629	            for j, tx in enumerate(block.transactions):
630	                self._validate_transaction(path, tx)
631	                stored_tx_id = txs_raw[j].get("tx_id") if isinstance(txs_raw[j], dict) else None
632	                if stored_tx_id != tx.tx_id:
633	                    fail(
634	                        f"transaction in block {block.height} has a mismatched "
635	                        f"tx_id (stored {stored_tx_id!r}, recomputed {tx.tx_id})"
636	                    )
637	                if tx.tx_id in seen_tx_ids:
638	                    fail(
639	                        f"duplicate transaction {tx.tx_id} in block "
640	                        f"{block.height}"
641	                    )
642	                seen_tx_ids.add(tx.tx_id)
643	                tx_ids.append(tx.tx_id)
644	            # Blocks store transactions in ascending tx_id order.
645	            if tx_ids != sorted(tx_ids):
646	                fail(f"block {block.height} transactions are not tx_id sorted")
647	
648	            recomputed_merkle = crypto.merkle_root(tx_ids)
649	            if recomputed_merkle != block.merkle_root:
650	                fail(f"block {block.height} Merkle root mismatch")
651	            recomputed_hash = compute_block_hash(
652	                block.height, block.prev_hash, block.merkle_root
653	            )
654	            if recomputed_hash != block.block_hash:
655	                fail(f"block {block.height} block_hash mismatch")
656	            chain.append(block)
657	
658	        # Mempool: well-formed, no internal duplicates, never overlapping the
659	        # chain (neither confirmed nor pending-block transactions).
660	        pending: dict[str, Transaction] = {}
661	        pending_raw = data.get("pending", [])
662	        if not isinstance(pending_raw, list):
663	            fail("'pending' must be a list")
664	        for tx_raw in pending_raw:
665	            if not isinstance(tx_raw, dict):
666	                fail("pending entry is not a JSON object")
667	            try:
668	                tx = Transaction.from_dict(tx_raw)
669	            except (KeyError, TypeError, ValueError) as exc:
670	                fail(f"pending transaction is malformed: {exc}")
671	            self._validate_transaction(path, tx)
672	            if tx_raw.get("tx_id") != tx.tx_id:
673	                fail(
674	                    f"pending transaction has a mismatched tx_id (stored "
675	                    f"{tx_raw.get('tx_id')!r}, recomputed {tx.tx_id})"
676	                )
677	            if tx.tx_id in pending:
678	                fail(f"duplicate pending transaction {tx.tx_id} in mempool")
679	            if tx.tx_id in seen_tx_ids:
680	                fail(
681	                    f"pending transaction {tx.tx_id} already exists in a block"
682	                )
683	            pending[tx.tx_id] = tx
684	
685	        # Cross-check the persisted tip summary against the chain tail.
686	        tip = chain[-1]
687	        if state.get("height") is not None and state["height"] != tip.height:
688	            fail("state.height does not match the chain tip")
689	        if state.get("tip_hash") is not None and state["tip_hash"] != tip.block_hash:
690	            fail("state.tip_hash does not match the chain tip")
691	        if (
692	            state.get("tip_status") is not None
693	            and state["tip_status"] != tip.status
694	        ):
695	            fail("state.tip_status does not match the chain tip")
696	
697	        # The recorded endowment is the *only* balance-replay parameter for the
698	        # persisted fork candidates: revalidation below must use it rather than
699	        # this instance's constructor argument, so starting with a different
700	        # --initial-balance can never change a fork's legality. Only a legacy
701	        # snapshot that records no endowment falls back to the configured (then
702	        # the default) value; every snapshot written by current code records it.
703	        replay_endowment = initial_balance
704	        if replay_endowment is None:
705	            replay_endowment = (
706	                self.initial_balance
707	                if self.initial_balance is not None
708	                else DEFAULT_INITIAL_BALANCE
709	            )
710	
711	        forks = self._parse_persisted_forks(
712	            data.get("forks", []), chain, replay_endowment
713	        )
714	        # The trust registry is authoritative configuration and must be parsed
715	        # before the sync records, whose sources are re-authorized against it.
716	        trust_sources = self._parse_persisted_trust_sources(
717	            data.get("trust_sources", []), path
718	        )
719	        # Parse the durable append-only audit log verbatim. It must NOT be
720	        # mutated here: same-generation snapshot conflict detection compares
721	        # parsed audit events, and a time-dependent backfill would make two
722	        # byte-identical snapshots look conflicting. The expired-record
723	        # reconciliation returned below is applied once, by load(), to the
724	        # single winning snapshot.
725	        audit_events = self._parse_persisted_audit_events(
726	            data.get("audit_events", []), path
727	        )
728	        audit_checkpoint, audit_repair = self._assess_audit_chain(
729	            data, audit_events, path
730	        )
731	        signer_state = self._parse_persisted_audit_signer(
732	            state, chain, audit_events, audit_checkpoint, path, state_version
733	        )
734	        syncs, expired_records, synced_tips = self._parse_persisted_syncs(
735	            data.get("syncs", []), forks, chain, trust_sources
736	        )
737	        # A fork brought in only by a sync record loses its right to exist once
738	        # that record is gone (expired/unauthorized/invalid on restart):
739	        # without this, the independently-persisted fork would resurrect as a
740	        # never-expiring candidate. Direct submissions carry no sync record and
741	        # are untouched.
742	        live_tips = {rec["tip_hash"] for rec in syncs.values()}
743	        canonical_hashes = {block.block_hash for block in chain}
744	        for tip in synced_tips - live_tips - canonical_hashes:
745	            forks.pop(tip, None)
746	        allowlist = self._parse_persisted_allowlist(data.get("allowlist", {}), path)
747	        return (
748	            chain,
749	            pending,
750	            generation,
751	            forks,
752	            initial_balance,
753	            syncs,
754	            trust_sources,
755	            allowlist,
756	            audit_events,
757	            expired_records,
758	            audit_checkpoint,
759	            audit_repair,
760	            signer_state,
761	        )

763	    @staticmethod
764	    def _assess_audit_chain(
765	        data: dict, audit_events: list[dict], path: str
766	    ) -> tuple[dict, bool]:
767	        """Validate the persisted audit hash chain and checkpoint.
768	
769	        Returns ``(checkpoint, needs_repair)``. Three cases:
770	
771	        * a current snapshot with complete hash links: every dense id,
772	          prev_hash link and event_hash is recomputed and the persisted
773	          ``audit_checkpoint`` must pin the exact log head — any mismatch is
774	          snapshot corruption and fails recovery;
775	        * a legacy snapshot predating hash chaining (no link fields, no
776	          checkpoint, or a checkpoint-less section): accepted for a one-time
777	          repair performed by load() on the unique winner; the checkpoint
778	          returned here is the would-be head so same-generation conflict
779	          comparison stays content-based;

861	            # predate both; anything else is corruption, never a reset.
862	            if raw is None and history_raw is not None:
863	                fail("audit_signer_history present without an audit_signer")
864	            if history_raw is None and raw is not None:
865	                fail("audit_signer present without an audit_signer_history")
866	            if state_version is not None and state_version < STATE_VERSION:
867	                return None, [], True
868	            if state_version is None:
869	                fail(
870	                    "snapshot without a state.version is missing both "
871	                    "audit_signer and audit_signer_history"
872	                )
873	            fail(
874	                f"snapshot at state.version {state_version} is missing both "

876	            )

881	        public_key = raw.get("public_key")

885	            or not isinstance(version, int)

890	            fail("audit_signer.private_key must be 64 lowercase hex chars")
891	        if not crypto.is_hex64(public_key):
892	            fail("audit_signer.public_key must be 64 lowercase hex chars")

894	            fail("audit_signer private_key does not derive its public_key")

901	            if not isinstance(entry, dict):
902	                fail("audit_signer_history entry must be an object")

905	            h_activated = entry.get("activated_event_id")
906	            if (
907	                isinstance(h_version, bool)
908	                or not isinstance(h_version, int)

943	        # key; every such event must in turn match a history entry.

957	                event.get("version") != entry["version"]

985	        current = {

993	    @staticmethod
994	    def _backfill_expired_events(
995	        audit_events: list[dict],
996	        expired_records: list[tuple[str, str, dict]],
997	    ) -> int:
998	        """Append one sync_expired event per down-time-expired sync record.
999	
1000	        Mirrors the runtime sweep exactly: records are processed in
1001	        ``(source, request_id)`` order, each gets a dense event_id continuing
1002	        after the durable history, and every *lifecycle removal* gets its own
1003	        event. Deduplication is lifecycle-aware, never identity-based across
1004	        lifecycles: a durable sync_expired covers the persisted record only
1005	        when it sits after the latest sync_received for the same
1006	        ``(source, request_id)`` key — i.e. it belongs to the record's
1007	        current lifecycle (the crash-interrupted-cleanup case). An expiry
1008	        event from an *earlier* lifecycle of a reused key never suppresses
1009	        the new lifecycle's event, even when source, request_id, tip_hash
1010	        and expires_at are all identical. Returns the number of events
1011	        appended. Mutates ``audit_events`` in place.
1012	        """
1013	        # Position of the latest sync_received per key: it opens the
1014	        # lifecycle every later event of that key belongs to.
1015	        last_received: dict[tuple[object, object], int] = {}
1016	        for index, event in enumerate(audit_events):
1017	            if event.get("kind") == EVENT_SYNC_RECEIVED:
1018	                last_received[(event.get("source"), event.get("request_id"))] = index
1019	        # Identities already expired *within their current lifecycle*.
1020	        covered: set[tuple[object, object, object]] = set()
1021	        for index, event in enumerate(audit_events):
1022	            if event.get("kind") != EVENT_SYNC_EXPIRED:
1023	                continue
1024	            key = (event.get("source"), event.get("request_id"))
1025	            if index > last_received.get(key, -1):
1026	                covered.add((key[0], key[1], event.get("tip_hash")))
1027	        backfilled = 0
1028	        for source, request_id, rec in sorted(
1029	            expired_records, key=lambda item: (item[0], item[1])
1030	        ):
1031	            identity = (source, request_id, rec["tip_hash"])
1032	            if identity in covered:
1033	                continue
1034	            event = {
1035	                "event_id": len(audit_events) + 1,
1036	                "kind": EVENT_SYNC_EXPIRED,
1037	                "at": time.time(),
1038	                "source": source,
1039	                "request_id": request_id,
1040	                "tip_hash": rec["tip_hash"],
1041	                "expires_at": rec["expires_at"],
1042	            }
1043	            # Freeze the delivered summary when recovery could resolve it;
1044	            # records in snapshots older than the frozen-summary feature may
1045	            # not carry one, in which case the history query resolves live.
1046	            if rec.get("height") is not None:
1047	                event["height"] = rec["height"]
1048	                event["length"] = rec.get("length")
1049	                event["status"] = rec.get("status")
1050	            audit_events.append(event)
1051	            covered.add(identity)
1052	            backfilled += 1
1053	        return backfilled

1059	        """Strictly parse the persisted source-trust registry.

1062	        the trust registry is authoritative configuration: a malformed entry
1063	        is snapshot corruption and fails recovery rather than being dropped.
1064	        Each record needs a non-empty source, a 64-char lowercase hex public
1065	        key, an integer expiry, a positive integer version and a known status.
1066	        """

1068	            return {}
1069	        if not isinstance(raw, list):
1070	            raise StateRecoveryError(path, "'trust_sources' must be a list")
1071	        sources: dict[str, dict] = {}
1072	        for entry in raw:
1073	            if not isinstance(entry, dict):
1074	                raise StateRecoveryError(path, "trust source entry must be an object")
1075	            source = entry.get("source")
1076	            public_key = entry.get("public_key")
1077	            expires_at = entry.get("expires_at")
1078	            version = entry.get("version")
1079	            status = entry.get("status")
1080	            if not isinstance(source, str) or not source:
1081	                raise StateRecoveryError(path, "trust source must be a non-empty string")
1082	            if not crypto.is_hex64(public_key):
1083	                raise StateRecoveryError(
1084	                    path, f"trust source {source!r} has an invalid public_key"
1085	                )
1086	            if isinstance(expires_at, bool) or not isinstance(expires_at, int):
1087	                raise StateRecoveryError(
1088	                    path, f"trust source {source!r} expires_at must be an integer"
1089	                )
1090	            if (
1091	                isinstance(version, bool)
1092	                or not isinstance(version, int)
1093	                or version < 1
1094	            ):
1095	                raise StateRecoveryError(
1096	                    path, f"trust source {source!r} version must be a positive integer"
1097	                )
1098	            if status not in (TRUST_ACTIVE, TRUST_REVOKED):
1099	                raise StateRecoveryError(
1100	                    path, f"trust source {source!r} has invalid status {status!r}"
1101	                )
1102	            if source in sources:
1103	                raise StateRecoveryError(
1104	                    path, f"duplicate trust source {source!r} in snapshot"
1105	                )
1106	            sources[source] = {
1107	                "public_key": public_key,
1108	                "expires_at": expires_at,
1109	                "version": version,
1110	                "status": status,
1111	            }

1239	    def _parse_persisted_syncs(
1240	        self,
1241	        syncs_raw: object,
1242	        forks: dict[str, list[Block]],
1243	        canonical_chain: list[Block],
1244	        trust_sources: dict[str, dict] | None = None,
1245	    ) -> tuple[dict[tuple[str, str], dict], list[tuple[str, str, dict]], set[str]]:
1246	        """Parse persisted sync records, dropping unusable ones on restart.
1247	
1248	        A record is kept only when it is structurally valid, has not yet
1249	        expired, its source is still an active, unexpired entry of the
1250	        persistent trust registry, and its tip references either a surviving
1251	        candidate fork or a block on the canonical chain (a synced candidate
1252	        may have been adopted). Records that expire while the process is down,
1253	        or whose source is unknown/revoked/registry-expired, are pruned and
1254	        additionally returned as ``expired_records`` (each as
1255	        ``(source, request_id, {tip_hash, expires_at, fingerprint})``) so the
1256	        caller backfills one sync_expired audit event per record — mirroring
1257	        the runtime sweep. Other staleness (malformed structure, a record
1258	        pointing at neither surviving location, or a fingerprint that no
1259	        longer matches the delivered candidate) is a silent orphan prune with
1260	        no event; duplicated keys keep the first copy. Invalid records are
1261	        silently dropped rather than failing recovery of the canonical chain.
1262	        The historical sync_received/sync_adopted/sync_expired audit events
1263	        are never touched by this pruning. Also returns the set of every tip
1264	        any sync record claims provenance for (including dropped ones), so the
1265	        caller can drop forks that only a pruned sync kept alive.
1266	        """
1267	        if not isinstance(syncs_raw, list):
1268	            return {}, [], set()
1269	        now = time.time()
1270	        trust_sources = trust_sources or {}
1271	        # Map every canonical block hash to the chain prefix ending there:
1272	        # this is the exact "candidate" document that was delivered for a tip
1273	        # since adopted onto the canonical chain.
1274	        canonical_prefixes: dict[str, list[dict]] = {}
1275	        prefix: list[dict] = []
1276	        for block in canonical_chain:
1277	            prefix = prefix + [block.to_dict()]
1278	            canonical_prefixes[block.block_hash] = prefix
1279	        syncs: dict[tuple[str, str], dict] = {}
1280	        expired_records: list[tuple[str, str, dict]] = []
1281	        synced_tips: set[str] = set()
1282	        for rec_raw in syncs_raw:
1283	            if not isinstance(rec_raw, dict):
1284	                continue
1285	            source = rec_raw.get("source")
1286	            request_id = rec_raw.get("request_id")
1287	            tip_hash = rec_raw.get("tip_hash")
1288	            expires_at = rec_raw.get("expires_at")
1289	            fingerprint = rec_raw.get("fingerprint")
1290	            if not isinstance(source, str) or not source:
1291	                continue
1292	            if not isinstance(request_id, str) or not request_id:
1293	                continue
1294	            if not crypto.is_hex64(tip_hash):
1295	                continue
1296	            # The frozen tip summary is optional for snapshots written before
1297	            # it was persisted; when present it must be structurally sound.
1298	            frozen_height = rec_raw.get("height")
